name: Benny and Scotty Enter the Building
description: Benny and Scotty walk through the entrance of a building and step inside together.
related_events: Benny and Scotty enter a building

name: Benny Reacts to a Jerk
description: Benny shakes his head, eyes narrowing as the person walks away. 'God, whadda jerk!' he mutters under his breath, clenching his fists briefly before turning in the other direction.
related_events: Benny expresses frustration toward someone

name: Mother Encourages Scotty to Ask for Help
description: Scotty's mother stands in the kitchen, quietly making coffee. She turns to Scotty and asks, "Well?..." Scotty replies, "He's too busy, Mom." She gently urges him, "Go back in there and ask. He'll take the time. Go on."
related_events: Mother encourages Scotty to ask for help

name: Scotty Enters the Outfield Through a Hidden Doorway
description: Scotty moves quietly through thick bushes, clutching a stack of books and a 'John Glenn - Freedom 7' lunchbox. He reaches a section of the fence where a small, concealed door is hidden. He opens it carefully and steps through, entering the distant outfield on the other side.
related_events: Scotty sneaks through a secret doorway in the fence onto the outfield

name: The Hairy Paw Takes the Baseball
description: A large, hairy paw descends from above, lands in the dirt, and scoops up the baseball from the small crater it had made. The paw lifts away, rising out of view. The crater remains, now empty.
related_events: Hairy paw removes baseball from dirt crater

name: Scotty Wakes Up Late and Rushes Out
description: Scotty wakes up and looks at his clock. It reads 8:30. He jumps out of bed, runs through the house, reaches the front door, opens it, and sprints outside.
related_events: Scotty wakes up and checks the time
Scotty rushes out of the house

name: Scotty and Benny Part Ways with a Glove Exchange
description: Scotty and Benny walk together until they reach the middle of the street, where they split off toward their respective homes. As Benny continues toward his house, already reaching his door, Scotty calls out and holds up Benny's glove. Benny raises his hand, still wearing one glove, and says, "Keep it," before going inside.
related_events: Scotty and Benny part ways in the middle of the street
Benny declines his glove and tells Scotty to keep it

name: Scotty Hits a Home Run and Benny Approves
description: DeNunez throws a fastball. Scotty swings and hits the ball hard. It flies over Squints' head in center field. In left field, Benny sees it and gives Scotty a thumbs up.
related_events: Scotty hits a home run off DeNunez's fastball
Benny gives Scotty a thumbs up from left field

name: Scotty Runs Past Familiar Places
description: Scotty runs through the neighborhood, passing a 5 & Dime, a Boys Club, and a Little League field. As he reaches the field, he slows, watching children in crisp uniforms playing on the diamond. He pauses for a moment, then continues on.
related_events: Scotty runs past familiar places
Scotty slows down at the Little League field

name: Bill Reacts to Scotty's Clanging Spoon
description: Scotty eats breakfast at the table, his spoon clanging against the bowl several times. Bill, sitting across and sifting through a pile of paperwork, looks up. Scotty says, 'Sorry,' then picks up his bowl and cereal and walks away.
related_events: Scotty's spoon clangs repeatedly during breakfast
Bill looks up at Scotty after being annoyed by the clanging
Scotty apologizes and leaves the table with his cereal

name: Scotty Sees Ham at the Bakery Truck
description: Scotty sees Ham buying a donut from the Helms Bakery truck down the block. Ham spots him and calls out, 'Hey-hey, come on! Wait up - wait up!' Scotty panics and runs back inside.
related_events: Scotty glimpses Ham buying a donut at the Helms Bakery truck
Ham calls out to Scotty to wait up
Scotty panics and runs back inside

name: Scotty Drinks Chocolate Quick and Crosses the House
description: Scotty drinks a glass of chocolate Quick and rinses it carefully. He takes a deep breath, then starts walking across the house.
related_events: Scotty drinks chocolate Quick and rinses the glass meticulously
Scotty gathers courage and begins walking across the house

name: Scotty's Glove Fails During Bill's Pitch
description: Bill throws a baseball toward Scotty during a practice session. Scotty raises his glove to catch it, but the webbing tears on impact. The ball passes through the glove and strikes Scotty in the eye.
related_events: Bill throws baseball toward Scotty
Scotty fails to catch baseball due to broken glove
Baseball hits Scotty in the eye

name: Scotty Follows the Group at School's End
description: At the end of the 5th grade, a flood of children rushed through the school entrance, their tennis shoes scuffing the floor and lunch boxes clattering. Amid the noise and motion, Scotty spotted eight boys moving together ahead of the crowd. He fell in behind them and followed as they made their way down the corridor.
related_events: Group of kids enters school building at end of 5th grade
Scotty follows a group of eight boys

name: Scotty knocks on the door and enters as Bill responds
description: Scotty stands near a slightly open door, watching Bill move around inside as he unpacks boxes. He reaches out as if to knock, then pulls back, turns away, and takes a few steps to leave. He stops, turns back, and after a moment, knocks on the door. From inside, Bill says, 'Yeah...' Scotty then takes a few cautious steps into the room.
related_events: Scotty hesitates before knocking on the door
Scotty knocks on the door
Bill responds to the knock from inside the room
Scotty enters the room cautiously

name: Students Leave Classroom After Bell Rings
description: The school bell rings. Benny, Ham, Scotty, and the other students immediately get up and head for the door. As they rush out, papers are knocked loose from desks and drift to the floor.
related_events: School bell rings to mark end of term
Students leave classroom after bell rings
Papers fall to the floor during classroom departure

name: Maury Wills Steals Third Base and Sparks a Legend
description: Maury Wills crouched low at second base, then in a flash he took off, sprinting toward third. The pitcher turned and threw hard to the bag, but Wills slid in just before the ball arrived. The third baseman fumbled the dirt, and the umpire, after a beat, raised his hand high. Safe. Wills rose, dusted off his cleats, and trotted back to the base. Later, that same cleat—the one he wore during the steal—became the model for the P.F. Flyer sneaker.
related_events: Maury Wills steals third base
Umpire calls Maury Wills safe
Maury Wills' cleat becomes the P.F. Flyer sneaker

name: The Fortress and the Disappearance
description: Mertle's Acres Junkyard stands transformed into a gothic fortress of scrap metal and rusted machinery, its twisted structures shaped over years by the imaginations of children. The towering piles of wreckage form walls that seem designed not to keep intruders out, but to contain something within. SQUINTS (V.O.) recalls that the Beast belongs to Mr. Mertle, the man who once owned the junkyard. No one has seen Mr. Mertle since the day something happened among the heaps of metal and shadowed corridors of his fortress. The place remains, silent and watchful, as the stories grow.
related_events: Junkyard is transformed into a gothic scrapyard fortress
Mr. Mertle disappears after the incident at the junkyard

name: Benny Teaches Scotty to Hit Bottle Caps
description: Benny shows Scotty the correct way to stand and swing a bat. Then, standing nearby, he flips bottle caps one by one from a coffee can, sending them spinning toward Scotty. At first, the caps are hard to hit, but Scotty adjusts quickly. One by one, he starts making contact, swinging cleanly and accurately. By the end, every cap that flies toward him is met with a sharp crack of the imaginary bat, each one struck cleanly. The sun sinks low in the sky, casting long shadows as the last cap is flicked and hit, and the practice session comes to an end.
related_events: Benny teaches Scotty proper batting stance and swing technique
Benny flicks bottle caps at Scotty for batting practice
Scotty successfully hits every bottle cap flicked by Benny
Sun sets during Benny and Scotty's practice session

name: Benny Goes Home Under the Full Moon
description: Benny walks into his house. Behind him, the others are still far off, just beginning to round the corner. The full moon hangs in the sky, bright and round like a baseball, casting light over the neighborhood.
related_events: Benny enters his house while others lag behind

name: Benny Stands with His Friends
description: During youth league tryouts, all the boys made the teams, but were assigned to different ones. Benny told them that if they couldn't play together, they shouldn't play at all. The others agreed, and they stayed together.
related_events: Benny refuses to play on separate teams

name: Benny Watches Scotty Duck a Thrown Ball
description: Benny comes out of his house and stands on the sidewalk, looking up the side of Scotty's house toward the backyard. He sees Scotty standing alone, trying to catch balls that are coming at him quickly. A ball flies toward Scotty, who ducks just in time. The ball hits the concrete wall behind him and bounces back in the direction of where someone—perhaps Bill—must be standing. Benny watches, taking it all in.
related_events: Benny exits his house and observes Scotty in the backyard
Scotty attempts to catch fast-moving balls in the backyard
Ball strikes wall after Scotty ducks
Benny draws incorrect conclusion about the situation

name: Mr. Mertle Walks The Beast Through the Neighborhood
description: People slammed their windows shut and pulled the curtains closed. Parents grabbed their children and rushed inside, locking the doors behind them. Mr. Mertle walked down the street holding a heavy chain attached to The Beast, whose form remained mostly out of view.
related_events: Residents secure their homes in response to The Beast's presence
Mr. Mertle walks The Beast on a heavy chain

name: The Beast Is Led Away
description: People slam their windows shut and pull the curtains closed. Parents grab their children and rush inside, locking the doors behind them. Mr. Mertle walks forward, guiding The Beast on a heavy chain. Though only parts of The Beast are visible, his presence is felt. There are no bones, no teeth, no evidence left behind.
related_events: The Beast is retired from guard duty due to excessive effectiveness

name: Scotty Starts a Baseball Memory List
description: Scotty opens a digital writing tablet and creates a new page. He types the title 'Baseball Stuff to Remember' at the top. Below it, he writes '1. The Great Bambino?' and stops, unsure of the answer.
related_events: Scotty opens a new writing tablet
Scotty titles the page 'Baseball Stuff to Remember'

name: Scotty Writes About The Great Bambino
description: Scotty opens a new writing tablet and titles the page 'Baseball Stuff to Remember.' He writes the first item: '1. The Great Bambino?' and pauses, unsure of who the nickname refers to.
related_events: Scotty writes '1. The Great Bambino?' on the page
Scotty shows confusion about 'The Great Bambino'

name: Scott Searches for Baseball Gear in His Closet
description: Scott takes off his cowboy pajamas and puts on regular clothes. He opens his closet and starts searching through it, pulling out a packaged toy baseball glove. A note attached to the package reads: 'To Scotty Boy - Love, Grandma!' He sets the glove aside and continues looking, digging through a pair of Mickey Mouse ears and a cowboy hat. Finally, he finds a long, duck-billed fishing cap with a big embroidered trout and takes it out, placing it with the glove.
related_events: Scott removes cowboy pajamas and redresses
Scott searches closet for baseball glove
Scott discovers note on packaged glove
Scott rummages through costume items
Scott selects fishing cap as substitute baseball cap

name: Benny and the Baseball
description: Benny stands at the window, gripping a baseball, looking toward Scotty's house. The narrator recalls that Benny was the only one who ever felt sorry for him when he was seen as a weenie. Neither of them knew it then, but their paths were set for one moment when the narrator would suffer a humiliating failure and Benny would come to his rescue. They drift off, Benny staring at a picture of Maury Wills caught in a pickle.
related_events: Narrator reflects on connection with Benny
Narrator describes shared destiny with Benny

name: Benny at the Window with a Baseball
description: Benny stands at the window, clutching a baseball, his eyes fixed on Scotty's house. The ball presses tightly in his hand as he watches the house without moving.
related_events: Benny clutches baseball while staring at Scotty's house

name: Scotty's Mom Reacts to His Eye Injury
description: Scotty's mom rushes over when she sees him holding his eye, demanding to know what happened. Scotty says it was because he took his eye off the ball. She pulls his hand away to look and sees a bad bruise forming. Bill takes a raw steak from the fridge, slaps it onto Scotty's eye, and tells him to keep it there for an hour to keep the swelling down. He adds that it will still be black, but it won’t get worse, then apologizes and says they’ll try again soon.
related_events: Scotty's mom reacts with alarm to Scotty's injury
Scotty explains the cause of his injury
Scotty's mom removes his hand from his eye
Bill applies raw steak to Scotty's injured eye
Bill offers reassurance and plans for future attempt

name: Yeah-Yeah Pees in the Spigots
description: Yeah-Yeah taps each of the three water spigots, urinating into them one by one. Ham, Squints, and Benny approach to drink. Yeah-Yeah calls out, "Milk-milk-pee," as he finishes. Ham, desperate for water, moves toward one of the spigots. Benny warns him it might not be safe, but Ham insists. Benny refuses to switch places with him. The others drink from the two spigots they believe are clean, leaving Ham to drink last. As they turn away, Scotty steps up to the fountain and takes a long drink from the contaminated spigot. The group gags and pretends to vomit, laughing. Scotty looks at them, confused, not understanding why they’re reacting.
related_events: Yeah-Yeah contaminates water spigots with urine
Ham attempts to drink from contaminated spigot
Benny refuses to switch drinking positions with Ham

name: Scotty Drinks from the Pee Spigot
description: After the others finish drinking and turn to leave, Scotty walks over to the fountain. He leans in and takes a drink from one of the spigots. The group watches and immediately reacts with exaggerated gags and fake barfs, laughing. Scotty looks up, confused, not understanding why they are laughing at him.
related_events: Scotty drinks from the pee-contaminated spigot
Group reacts with mock disgust to Scotty's drinking

name: Benny Takes Items and Leaves the Soda Fountain
description: Benny grabs a baseball and a handful of chewing gum from the jar on the soda fountain counter. He places money on the counter and walks out. Scotty follows behind him.
related_events: Benny takes a baseball and chewing gum from the soda fountain counter
Benny leaves money on the soda fountain counter
Benny exits the soda fountain area

name: Scotty Follows Benny Out of the Soda Fountain
description: Benny leaves the soda fountain counter after placing money down and taking a baseball and some bazooka from a jar. He walks out. Scotty follows behind him.
related_events: Scotty follows Benny out of the soda fountain area

name: The Room Full of Baseball
description: The room was covered in pennants, magazine pictures, game programs, and baseball cards, with an entire section dedicated to Maury Wills, centered on a photo of him caught in a rundown. The narrator stood quietly, taking it in. Outside, Benny lay in bed, rubbing oil into his glove, his eyes fixed on Scotty's house across the way. Taped to the footboard of his bed was a picture of The Babe, the most important one of all. The narrator had never played baseball before moving in that summer, but after a week of watching the others, he began to understand what mattered here.
related_events: Narrator observes baseball memorabilia in the room
Narrator reflects on future significance of the location
Narrator realizes baseball is key to fitting in

name: Benny Oils His Glove and Looks Toward Scotty's House
description: Benny sits in bed, rubbing oil into his baseball glove. He stares out the window toward Scotty's house. Taped to the footboard of his bed is a picture of Babe Ruth.
related_events: Benny oils his baseball glove in bed
Benny displays revered picture of The Babe

name: Squints Brings the Box, Cards Are Drawn
description: Squints arrived with a shoebox of baseball cards. He shook the box, then held it out. One by one, the group reached in and pulled out a card. Each card had a player’s name, and whoever was picked became the person you played as when it was your turn.
related_events: Squints arrives with a box of baseball cards
Squints shakes up the box of baseball cards
Group members draw baseball cards from the box

name: Ham's Serious Pick and the Terrifying Secret
description: Every morning, the group gathered around a shoebox filled with baseball cards they called 'The Dugout.' Squints shook the box, and each boy drew a card, becoming that player when it was their turn to be up. One day, Ham reached in and pulled out his card with an unusual intensity, holding it silently, his expression serious. The others noticed the shift. Without a word, they exchanged glances, then turned to the narrator. In hushed voices, they began to reveal a secret—one they called the world's most terrifying—drawing the narrator into something deeper than the usual game.
related_events: Ham takes his card pick too seriously
Guys reveal a terrifying secret to the narrator

name: Scotty Asks Bill to Play Catch
description: Scotty stands in the trophy room, watching Bill dust a batting trophy and adjust a pitching plaque. He hesitates, then asks if Bill remembers promising to teach him how to play catch. Bill looks up briefly, gives a vague acknowledgment, and says, 'Sure.' Scotty waits, but Bill turns back to the shelf without saying more. Scotty says, 'Okay. Great. Thanks,' and starts to leave. As he pulls the door closed, he glances back and sees Bill place a silver pedestal on the main shelf and carefully set an ordinary baseball on top.
related_events: Scotty gathers courage to speak in the trophy room
Scotty asks Bill to teach him how to play catch
Bill acknowledges Scotty's request with minimal response
Scotty expresses disappointment and leaves the trophy room
Bill places a baseball on a silver pedestal in the trophy room

name: The Family's Early Days with Bill
description: The narrator recalls how his real father died when he was very young. About a year after his mother married Bill, the family moved to a new neighborhood. At the time, the relationship between Bill and the narrator's mother was still new, marked by hesitation and quiet adjustment.
related_events: Narrator's real father dies in early childhood
Mother marries Bill and family moves to new neighborhood
Bill and mother's relationship begins with hesitation and adjustment
Narrator reflects on early family history with Bill

name: Mr. Mertle Brings the Dog to Mertle's Acres
description: After more thefts at Mertle's Acres, Mr. Mertle goes to the pound and takes a dog they were eager to be rid of. The dog had killed three larger dogs during his time there. Mr. Mertle brings him back to the junkyard and sets him loose among the twisted vehicles, old appliances, and scrap piles. He throws a trash bag full of meat onto the ground each night and leaves the dog alone. The dog stays in the junkyard, moving through the dark passages, growing larger, his breath echoing among the wreckage.
related_events: Mr. Mertle acquires a new dog from the pound
Mr. Mertle releases The Beast into Mertle's Acres

name: The Beast Grows in the Junkyard
description: Each night, a trash bag full of meat is thrown into the junkyard. It lands with a thud, then vanishes into the dark maze of scrap. A moment later, the bag spits back into view—empty, torn, and shredded. The Beast moves through the piles of wreckage, his shoulders towering over rusted cars, his breath heavy in the still air. He grows larger, his footsteps leaving deep imprints in crushed tires, his form passing silently between broken appliances and mangled lawn ornaments. No one speaks to him. No one comes near. He is alone among the twisted metal and hollow shells, where the only sound is the tearing of flesh and the crunch of bone.
related_events: The Beast grows alone in the junkyard
The Beast consumes a trash bag of meat

name: The Beast Grows and Destroys
description: The pup left in Mertle's Acres grows rapidly, towering over wrecked cars and leaving deep footprints in crushed tires. Night after night, a trash bag full of meat is thrown into the dark passages and vanishes—later spat back out, torn and empty. Among the heaps of scrap, broken mannequins lie with chunks torn away, plastic flamingoes are twisted and mangled, a lawn jockey is decapitated, and a plastic cow has its legs gnawed off. Something moves through the maze of junk—large, low, powerful. Its breath rasps between the rusted shells of old vehicles. It knocks over shopping carts, crushes appliances, and leaves behind signs of its presence in the wreckage. The burned-out school bus, the scrap motorbikes, the gutted fighter plane—all stand amid the ruin, silent witnesses to what now roams the yard.
related_events: The Beast grows to enormous size in the junkyard
The Beast develops aggressive and hostile behavior

name: Scotty Sees Something Grab the Ball
description: Scotty snaps his head away from the hole and runs over to the gang. 'Something got the ball!' he says, visibly unnerve. The others look at him, then exchange silent glances. Without speaking, they all nod. They prepare for a campout.
related_events: Scotty reacts to something grabbing the ball
The gang exchanges concerned glances

name: Friends Go Home with Glove Slaps and Goodnights
description: The boys returned to their block and split off toward their houses. They slapped gloves and called out 'so-long' as they headed inside. One by one, they disappeared into their homes, leaving the street quiet. Scotty stood in his driveway, moving boxes into the garage, watching them leave. Benny was the last to go. From his porch, he saw Scotty and gave a small nod before going inside. The street lamps flickered on, casting soft white circles onto the sidewalks. From above, the circles looked like baseballs scattered across the neighborhood.
related_events: Friends part ways after returning to their homes

name: Scotty Watches the Boys Go Home
description: The boys split off toward their houses, slapping gloves and calling out goodbyes. Scotty stands in his driveway, carrying moving boxes into the garage. He watches as they walk away. Benny is the last to leave. From his porch, he nods slightly in Scotty's direction. The others disappear into their homes. The street lamps turn on, casting soft white circles onto the sidewalks. From above, the lights look like baseballs scattered across the neighborhood.
related_events: Scotty carries moving boxes to his garage

name: Benny Nods to Scotty from the Porch
description: The other boys had already split off toward their homes, slapping gloves and calling out goodbyes. Scotty stood in his driveway, shuttling moving boxes into the garage, watching them go. Benny lingered on his porch, the last one left. He saw Scotty watching and gave a small, quiet nod. Then he turned and went inside.
related_events: Benny nods to Scotty from his porch before going inside

name: The Street Lamps Come On
description: The boys walked off in different directions, calling goodnights, slapping gloves as they headed to their homes. Scotty stood in his driveway, moving boxes into the garage, watching them leave. Benny was the last to go, pausing on his porch. He saw Scotty and gave a small nod. Then he went inside. The block emptied out. One by one, the street lamps flicked on, casting soft white circles onto the sidewalks. From above, the circles looked like baseballs scattered across the neighborhood.
related_events: Street lamps illuminate the empty block

name: Ham Makes a Messy S'more
description: Ham gathered the group around the Cub Scout camping stove and showed them how to make a s'more. He placed a piece of Hershey's chocolate on a graham cracker, then held a marshmallow over the flame to roast it. The marshmallow suddenly caught fire, flaring up in the heat. Ham quickly pulled it off and pressed it onto the chocolate, sandwiching it with another graham cracker. He took a big bite, eating it eagerly, but the hot, gooey filling oozed out and dripped down his shirt, leaving a sticky mess.
related_events: Ham demonstrates how to make a s'more
Marshmallow catches fire during roasting
Ham eats a s'more and gets messy

name: Squints Tells the Legend of The Beast
description: Squints turned the lantern down low and told the group to listen. He said that when DeNunez first heard the story, he fainted. DeNunez protested, calling it a lie, but Benny confirmed it was true. Squints went on, saying that Yeah-Yeah had once peed his pants while hearing it. Yeah-Yeah denied it, but Ham backed up the claim. Then Squints said that Ham himself had thrown up two bags of marshmallows after hearing the tale. Ham argued it was only one. With the group restless and arguing, Squints warned them to stay away from the door and not to sit on their sleeping bags, or they might fall out or soil themselves. He called for silence, and the boys quieted down, watching him in the dim light. He began: the legend of The Beast went back a long time, before any of them could even pick up a baseball, to a place called Mertle's Acres.
related_events: Squints dimly lights the lantern to begin storytelling
DeNunez denies fainting at the story's previous telling
Yeah-Yeah denies peeing his pants during the story
Ham disputes vomiting two bags of marshmallows
Squints recounts the legend of The Beast

name: Detectives Question Mr. Mertle About Missing Thieves
description: Detectives speak with Mr. Mertle, showing him file photos of thieves in ski masks. His shoulders slumped and his eyes moist, Mr. Mertle listens in silence. Later, police begin receiving phone calls from people reporting the disappearances of numerous thieves—thirty-seven in total—linked to The Beast. Mr. Mertle walks solemnly into the junkyard and then emerges, followed by something at the end of a rusty tow chain. The officers take cover behind their cars, aiming their guns at him and whatever comes after.
related_events: Detectives show file photos of thieves in ski masks to Mr. Mertle
Police receive phone calls reporting missing thieves linked to The Beast

name: Mr. Mertle Emerges with The Beast
description: Mr. Mertle walked slowly into the junkyard, his shoulders slumped, his eyes moist. After a time, he came out again, followed by a massive dog at the end of a rusty tow chain. The dog moved behind him, silent and heavy. Police officers, already on scene, ducked behind their cars and raised their guns, aiming at Mr. Mertle and the animal now standing beside him.
related_events: Mr. Mertle solemnly enters the junkyard
Mr. Mertle emerges from the junkyard followed by The Beast on a tow chain

name: Police Confront Mr. Mertle and The Beast
description: Mr. Mertle emerged from the junkyard, walking slowly as The Beast followed behind him, tethered to a rusty tow chain. The officers, standing near their patrol cars, quickly ducked for cover behind the vehicles. Guns were drawn and aimed steadily at Mr. Mertle and the massive dog moving at the end of the chain.
related_events: Police take cover behind their cars and aim guns at Mr. Mertle and The Beast

name: Squints Reveals What Happened to the Thieves
description: Squints speaks in voiceover as Mr. Mertle walks into the junkyard. He says The Beast ate the thieves—every last one of them, bones and all. Police stand behind their cars with guns drawn as Mr. Mertle reappears, leading something at the end of a rusty tow chain.
related_events: Squints narrates that The Beast ate the thieves completely

name: Scotty Asks Bill for Catch Practice
description: Scotty returns and stands quietly near Bill. After a long pause, he hesitates, glancing toward the kitchen, and quietly says, 'Could we... I mean, could you teach me to catch today?' Bill looks up and replies, 'Um, yeah, but later, okay? I gotta get this done.' Scotty says, 'Okay, thanks.' Mom enters and asks Bill why he can't take a break to teach Scotty now. Scotty tries to interrupt, saying it's okay, but no one listens. Bill drops his pen, checks his watch, and says, 'Fine. Alright. I'll get my glove. Come on.' He walks past them. Scotty shuffles out, shaking his head, as Mom says, 'There. See. Told you so.'
related_events: Scotty requests Bill to teach him to catch
Bill postpones teaching Scotty to catch

name: Mom Insists Bill Teach Scotty Now
description: Mom enters and sees Scotty standing quietly near Bill. Without addressing Scotty, she turns to Bill and asks why he can’t take a break to teach him now. Bill responds that he said he would, but needs to finish his work first. Mom presses him, saying it shouldn’t take long and questioning if he can’t spare even half an hour. Bill drops his pen, checks his watch, and agrees with annoyance, saying fine, he’ll get his glove. He tells Scotty to come on and walks out. Scotty shuffles after him, avoiding his mother’s gaze. Mom looks at Scotty, satisfied, and says, 'There. See. Told you so.'
related_events: Mom confronts Bill about teaching Scotty to catch

name: Bill Agrees to Play Catch
description: After a pause, Bill drops his pen, checks his watch, and says he will teach Scotty to catch. He tells Scotty to come on and walks past them out of the room. Scotty shuffles toward the back, following.
related_events: Bill gives in and agrees to teach Scotty immediately
Bill exits to get his glove for playing catch

name: Scotty's Embarrassment After Mom's Intervention
description: Scotty stands quietly as his mother speaks up, urging Bill to teach him to catch. He looks down, visibly uncomfortable. After Bill agrees with annoyance and heads inside to get his glove, Scotty shuffles toward the backyard, shaking his head. He does not respond to his mother as she watches, unaware.
related_events: Scotty reacts with embarrassment to Mom's intervention
Scotty leaves for the backyard in quiet disappointment

name: The Gang Prepares the Field
description: The gang worked together to get their homemade baseball diamond ready. They swept the bleachers with broken brooms, raked the infield using the halves of old tools, and poured detergent powder from a cracked box to mark fresh chalk lines. In the outfield, they gathered up leaves, trash, and sticks, clearing the ground for play. They lifted a piece of worn plywood back into place in left field, its surface painted green and labeled "The Green Monster." Nearby, Scotty stayed hidden, watching from cover as the boys finished their work. The gang took their positions on the field, tossing a ball back and forth, spreading out until each stood where he liked to play, fitting the rough shape of the makeshift diamond.
related_events: Gang cleans bleachers with broken brooms
Gang rakes infield with tool halves
Gang lays new chalk lines using detergent powder
Gang clears outfield of debris
Gang re-erects 'The Green Monster' plywood wall

name: The Gang Starts Playing Ball
description: The gang finishes working on the field and begins tossing a baseball back and forth on the homemade diamond. As they play catch, they slowly spread apart, each moving to a spot on the field where they like to play. Soon, they are standing in their usual positions—scrappy and ready—facing one another across the dirt infield, fully settled into the game.
related_events: Gang initiates game of catch on homemade diamond
Gang members position themselves for baseball play

name: The Hundred Days of Baseball
description: The gang gathers on their homemade baseball diamond, sweeping the bleachers with broken brooms, raking the infield with shattered tools, and pouring detergent powder from a cracked box to mark the chalk lines. They clear the outfield of leaves, trash, and sticks, then hoist a torn piece of plywood into place in left field—painted green and labeled "The Green Monster." Scotty watches from cover, eyeing the row of backyards lined with chain-link fences, some trimmed in wood, others in bamboo, one boasting a massive treehouse. Next door, the final yard is blocked off by tall panels of green privacy fiberglass lashed to the fence. He stays hidden, restless, but the others don’t notice. As they finish, Ham tosses a ball into the air and says, "Fifth grade's history, man. A hundred days, man. A hundred days of baseball." Timmy adds, "We got all summer," and the others echo him. Benny calls, "Let's play," and they begin tossing the ball around. They spread out across the field, each drifting to their usual position, settling into the dirt like they belong there, small and scrappy under the open sky.
related_events: Gang recalls hundred days of baseball tradition

name: Scotty Watches from Hiding
description: Scotty stays hidden, crouched behind cover near the edge of the yard. He watches the row of houses behind the baseball diamond, studying the backyards lined with chain-link fences. Each fence is trimmed differently—wood, bamboo—some with neat details, one with a treehouse that stands out. His eyes linger on the last house, where tall green fiberglass panels are lashed to the fence, blocking the yard. The gang works across the field, raking, sweeping, laying chalk lines with a torn box of detergent, re-erecting a ragged piece of plywood they call the Green Monster. They toss a ball around, spreading out into positions, laughing, settling into their game. Scotty stays still, not moving toward them, not calling out. He watches, close enough to hear, but never joins.
related_events: Scotty surveils backyard layout from cover
Scotty resists urge to join gang

name: The Beast Unmasks and Crushes the First Two Thieves
description: Two thieves in ski-masks are caught in a sudden blast of heated wind that rips their masks away. Before they can react, enormous elephantine feet slam down onto their faces, crushing them as they scream.
related_events: Heated wind strips masks from two thieves
Elephantine feet crush two thieves' faces

name: The Thief Dragged Into Darkness
description: A lone thief stands in the open when a shadow suddenly falls over him. Before he can react, the darkness surges forward, engulfing him completely. He is yanked off his feet and pulled into the blackness. A scream tears through the air, sharp and brief, then cuts off abruptly. There is no movement afterward, only silence.
related_events: Another thief is enveloped by shadow and dragged into darkness

name: The Van Crash and the Beast's Capture
description: Two thieves finish loading their van with stolen goods and speed away. The vehicle skids, loses control, and slams into an obstacle, crumpling violently. Before they can react, the Beast appears, tears open the wrecked van, and drags the two men out. They flail and babble incoherently, their faces twisted in terror as they are pulled away from the wreckage.
related_events: Two thieves load van and attempt escape
Van crashes in violent collision
Thieves dragged from wrecked van while blathering in horror

name: The Beast Attacks Mrtle's Acres
description: From high above Mrtle's Acres, the Beast moves like a murderous phantom, roaring with primordial bloodlust. Thieves in ski-masks scramble as their van suddenly skids and crumples in a violent crash. One pair is caught beneath elephantine feet that crush their faces into the ground. Another is swallowed by a shadow and dragged into darkness, screaming. Debris flies through the air—fake flamingos, a plastic cow—tossed aside as the Beast hurls thieves in every direction, leaving them blathering in horror.
related_events: Beast moves across Mrtle's Acres like a murderous phantom
Roaring and primordial bloodlust heard over Mrtle's Acres
Various thieves tossed around amid flying debris

name: Scotty's Contraption Hits Mom
description: Scotty tightens the last bolt on his Erector Set machine and flips the switch. A small motor whirs to life, powering a tiny scoop that lifts a white marble and sets it rolling down a track. The marble zips around curves and loops, lands in a miniature catapult, and is launched when a pair of scissors snips the restraining string. The marble flies over a little green fence and strikes his mother in the forehead just as she walks into the room. Scotty flinches at the impact and quickly says, 'Sorry, Mom.'
related_events: Scotty activates his Erector Set contraption
Marble from contraption hits Scotty's mother in the forehead
Scotty apologizes to his mother after hitting her with the marble

name: Mother Encourages Scotty to Play Outside
description: Scotty sits at his erector set table, finishing a small mechanical contraption. He flips a switch, and a tiny device lifts a white marble, sending it rolling down a track with loops and turns. The marble lands in a miniature catapult, which launches it over a little green fence. It strikes his mother in the forehead as she enters the room. She winces, and Scotty apologizes. She reminds him they had agreed to take the device apart and not spend so much time alone with it. She asks if he has made any friends, and he says no, explaining that he is still "new." She tells him she wants him to go outside, play, run, climb trees, hop fences, and even get into a little trouble. She says she is proud of him but wants him to make friends. Scotty reluctantly agrees. His mother suggests he might make friends the next day. He asks if his father will teach him to play catch, and she says he would love to, remembering how good he was at baseball in high school.
related_events: Mother expresses concern about Scotty's isolation and repetitive behavior
Scotty's mother encourages him to play outside and make friends

name: Scotty and His Mother Talk About Friends
description: Scotty's mother comes into his bedroom and sees him finishing a complex contraption made from an Erector Set. A small motor runs, sending a marble along a track that eventually launches it into the air. The marble hits her in the forehead. Scotty winces and apologizes. She reminds him they had agreed to take the project apart and spend less time alone in his room. She asks if he’s made any friends yet. He says no. She asks why, and he tells her it’s because he’s still 'new.' She urges him to go outside, play, get dirty, climb trees, and make friends. He says he doesn’t know how, and that he’s no good at anything. He calls himself an egghead. She replies that he’ll stay an egghead if he keeps thinking that way. He agrees to try. She suggests he might make friends tomorrow. He says maybe. Then he asks if his father will teach him to play catch. She says yes, that his father would love to, and reminds him how good his father was at baseball in high school.
related_events: Mother asks Scotty why he hasn't made any friends
Scotty explains he hasn't made friends because he's still "new"
Scotty expresses self-doubt and identifies himself as an egghead
Scotty's mother challenges his negative self-perception

name: Scotty Asks His Mother About Playing Catch with His Father
description: Scotty pauses, then asks his mother if his father, Bill, will teach him to play catch. His mother responds with enthusiasm, telling him Bill would love to, and mentions how Bill was a talented pitcher in college.
related_events: Scotty asks if his father will teach him to play catch
Scotty's mother reassures him about his father's willingness to bond

name: Scotty Promises to Make Friends
description: After his mother finds him alone in his room building an elaborate contraption that accidentally hits her in the forehead with a marble, Scotty apologizes and listens as she urges him to spend less time indoors and more time outside playing and making friends. She tells him she wants him to run around, get dirty, climb trees, and even get into a little trouble. Scotty hesitates, saying he doesn’t know how because he’s still new and feels like an egghead. His mother replies that he’ll stay that way if he doesn’t try, and asks him to promise. After a pause, he says, 'Okay.' She holds out hope that he might make some friends the next day. Scotty agrees, 'Yeah, maybe tomorrow.'
related_events: Scotty agrees to try to make friends

name: Bill Teaches Scotty to Catch
description: Bill slides his hand into his glove and pops the baseball into his palm, then tells Scotty to keep his eye on the ball and put the glove where it belongs. He throws the ball toward Scotty, who raises his glove to the right as the ball sails past to the left. Scotty retrieves the ball and runs back, handing it to Bill instead of throwing it. Bill checks his watch, then repeats the instruction. He throws again; the ball hits the edge of Scotty’s glove and breaks the webbing. Scotty looks at the damaged glove. Bill tells him to throw it back, and Scotty flips the ball weakly toward him.
related_events: Bill demonstrates proper catching technique to Scotty
Bill instructs Scotty to keep his eye on the ball and position the glove correctly

name: First Throw and Missed Catch
description: Bill throws a baseball to Scotty. Scotty raises his glove to the right, but the ball sails past on the left, missing the glove entirely. Bill tells him to keep his eye on the ball and to place the glove where the ball is going. Scotty retrieves the ball and runs back, handing it directly to Bill instead of throwing it. Bill checks his watch, then tosses the ball again toward Scotty. This time, the ball bounces off the glove, breaking the webbing.
related_events: Bill throws a baseball to Scotty
Scotty fails to catch Bill's throw
Bill throws the baseball again toward Scotty

name: Scotty Walks the Ball Back to Bill
description: Scotty retrieves the ball from the ground, then walks across the yard to Bill and hands it to him directly. Bill stares, checks his watch, and shakes his head slightly, his expression one of disbelief.
related_events: Scotty returns the ball by hand instead of throwing it
Bill expresses disbelief while checking his watch

name: Second Throw and Broken Glove
description: Bill throws the baseball again toward Scotty. The ball strikes the toy glove and bounces off, tearing the webbing. Scotty looks at the damaged glove and says, 'Darn. My glove got—' Bill interrupts, '—not bad. Right side at least. Now, just throw it back this time.'
related_events: Bill throws the baseball again toward Scotty
The baseball bounces off Scotty's toy glove and breaks the webbing
Scotty expresses disappointment about his damaged glove
Bill acknowledges partial success and instructs Scotty to throw the ball back

name: Scotty Flips the Ball Back, Bill Reacts in Shock
description: Scotty picks up the ball after it bounces off his glove, hesitates, then flips it weakly toward Bill. The ball tumbles short and low. Bill stares at the feeble attempt, his expression shifting to disbelief. He looks at his watch again, then mutters, 'Oh, my God.'
related_events: Scotty retrieves the ball and flips it back to Bill
Bill reacts with shock to Scotty's weak return flip
Bill expresses disbelief while checking his watch

name: The Police Set Rules for Containing The Beast
description: The police speak with Mr. Mertle and tell him he must keep The Beast locked in his backyard. They insist the animal be chained to prevent him from escaping and possibly harming children. A crane lowers a large bathtub into the yard, and firefighters begin filling it with water. Construction workers drive an I-beam deep into the ground, securing it with cement. Mr. Mertle builds a lean-to shelter from old, bullet-riddled tin signs. A welder fastens a heavy chain to the I-beam, and Mr. Mertle attaches the other end to a collar around The Beast’s neck. The Beast retreats under the lean-to, dust puffing up as he lies down. Mr. Mertle asks the officers how long he has to keep his dog chained like a slave.
related_events: Police instruct Mr. Mertle to confine The Beast in his backyard
Police require Mr. Mertle to chain up The Beast

name: Installing the I-Beam Anchor for The Beast's Chain
description: Construction workers drove an I-Beam girder into the ground. They filled the surrounding chasm with wet cement, which settled and hardened, securing the beam in place. A welder later attached a heavy chain to the girder, fastening it firmly.
related_events: Construction workers sink I-Beam girder into place
Cement fills chasm at construction site

name: Securing The Beast with the Chain
description: A welder fastens a heavy chain to the I-Beam girder embedded in the ground. Mr. Mertle takes the other end of the chain and fits it around The Beast's neck like a collar. The chain tightens, anchoring The Beast to the girder in the backyard.
related_events: Welder brazes chain to I-Beam girder
Mr. Mertle collars The Beast with chain

name: Mr. Mertle Builds a Shelter for The Beast
description: Mr. Mertle assembled a large lean-to in the backyard using old bullet-holed tin advertising signs. He secured a heavy chain to an I-beam embedded in the ground, attaching the other end to a collar around The Beast. The Beast moved beneath the shelter and lay down, the force of its body hitting the ground sending a burst of dust flying from underneath the structure.
related_events: Mr. Mertle constructs lean-to from old tin ads
The Beast retreats under lean-to shelter
Dust explodes from under lean-to as The Beast lies down

name: Lowering the Bathtub and Filling It with Water
description: A crane lowers a giant bathtub into Mr. Mertle's backyard. Firefighters arrive and begin filling the bathtub with water.
related_events: Crane lowers giant bathtub into Mr. Mertle's backyard
Firemen fill giant bathtub with water

name: Mr. Mertle Asks How Long The Beast Must Stay Chained
description: Squints speaks in voiceover, remembering the time Mr. Mertle asked the police how long he had to keep The Beast chained in the backyard. The police had required the chain to stay fastened to the I-beam, with The Beast confined beneath the lean-to made of old tin signs. Firemen had filled the bathtub with water, and the welder had secured the chain, but no one had said how long it would last.
related_events: Squints recalls Mr. Mertle questioning police about chaining duration

name: Ham Imitates Babe Ruth with a Candy Cigar
description: Ham chews on a candy cigar and strikes a pose, imitating Babe Ruth. 'Hey! Check me out! I'm the Great Bambino!' he announces. The gang laughs, enjoying the act. They exchange knowing glances, caught up in the moment of shared amusement.
related_events: Ham performs Babe Ruth imitation for the gang

name: The Gang Mocks Scotty for Not Knowing Babe Ruth
description: When Scotty asks who The Great Bambino is, the gang falls silent, then erupts in disbelief. Bertram demands if he was born in a barn. Yeah-Yeah and Squints mock him, asking what planet he's from. Tommy and Timmy shout titles like 'The Sultan of Swat' and 'The Colossus of Clout,' while Denunez adds 'The Titan of Terror.' Benny chimes in with 'The King of Krash.' Ham shudders at the mention of Bambi, calling him a wimpy deer. The others spit, unimpressed, while Scotty nervously dribbles the ball, clearly intimidated.
related_events: Scotty asks identity of The Great Bambino
Gang mocks Scotty for not knowing Babe Ruth

name: The Gang Recites Babe Ruth's Nicknames
description: Ham imitated Babe Ruth with a candy cigar, drawing laughter from the gang. Scotty asked who he was pretending to be, and the group fell silent, staring at him. Bertram asked if he was born in a barn. Another member mocked him for not knowing. Squints demanded if he'd never heard of the Sultan of Swat. Denunez called him the Titan of Terror. Timmy declared him the Colossus of Clout, and the others repeated it in unison. Benny, with his mouth full, added, 'The King of Krash.'
related_events: Gang members recite nicknames of Babe Ruth
Benny joins in with 'The King of Krash'

name: Scotty Pretends He Misheard
description: After asking who the Great Bambino was, Scotty tries to save face by saying he thought the name was 'The Great Bambi.' Ham shudders at the mention of Bambi, disgusted by the idea. The others in the group remain silent, unimpressed by Scotty's attempt to cover up his mistake.
related_events: Scotty falsely claims recognition of The Great Bambino
Ham reacts with disgust to mention of Bambi

name: The Gang Spits in Unison After Scotty's Mistake
description: After Scotty confuses 'The Great Bambino' with 'The Great Bambi,' the gang falls completely silent. Without a word, they all spit at once. Their eyes stay fixed on Scotty, who fidgets and dribbles the ball nervously.
related_events: Gang falls silent and spits to assert toughness

name: Benny Introduces Scotty to the Team
description: Benny stood with Scotty among the group and began naming each of the boys in turn. He pointed to Ken DeNunez, then Alan McClennan, whom they called Yeah-Yeah, then Hamilton Porter, known as Ham, followed by Tommy and Timmy Timmons, Bertram Grover Weeks, and Mike "Squints" Palledorus. After the introductions, Scotty raised a hand and said, "Hi." The others remained silent, watching him. Benny turned to the group and said Scotty would play with them, making nine—enough for a team.
related_events: Benny introduces gang members to Scotty
Scotty greets the gang
Benny announces Scotty will play with the gang

name: Benny Greets Scotty Across the Street
description: Scotty sits on the porch, chin in his hands, looking across the street. Benny stands on the curb opposite. When Scotty notices him, he startles and begins to cover his black eye before stopping himself. Benny raises a hand in greeting. After a moment, Scotty slowly waves back.
related_events: Scotty notices Benny across the street and reacts to his presence
Benny greets Scotty from across the street
Scotty returns Benny's greeting with a slow wave

name: Benny Crosses the Street to Invite Scotty to Play Baseball
description: Benny stepped off the curb, crossed the street, and walked over to where Scotty sat on the porch. He stood on the sidewalk and invited Scotty to play baseball. Scotty hesitated, then said no, explaining he didn’t have a glove.
related_events: Benny crosses the street to approach Scotty on the sidewalk
Benny invites Scotty to play baseball
Scotty declines Benny's invitation due to not having a glove

name: Benny Presses Scotty and Offers a Spare Glove
description: Scotty sits on the porch, chin in his hands, when Benny appears across the street. After a moment, Benny raises a hand in greeting. Scotty hesitates, then waves back. Benny crosses over and invites Scotty to play baseball. Scotty declines, saying he doesn’t have a glove. Benny presses him, asking why not if he likes the game. Scotty stammers and says his glove is busted. Benny reaches behind his back as if drawing a weapon, then smiles and pulls out a spare glove, offering it to Scotty. Scotty calls to his mom that he’s going to play ball, takes the glove, and thanks Benny, calling it cool. They begin walking down the block together.
related_events: Benny presses Scotty about not having a glove and questions his excuse
Benny dramatically produces a spare baseball glove from behind his back
Scotty accepts Benny's glove with gratitude

name: Scotty Accepts the Glove and Heads Out to Play
description: Scotty takes the glove Benny offers and calls out to his mother that he’s going to play ball. He turns away from the porch and starts walking down the sidewalk beside Benny, the new glove in his hand.
related_events: Scotty shouts to his mom that he's going to play ball

name: Scotty and Benny Head to the 5 & 10
description: As they walked down the block, Scotty thanked Benny again for the glove. Benny grinned and teased him about the black eye. He suggested stopping by the 5 & 10 to pick up a new baseball, some chewing tobacco, and other supplies. Scotty agreed, and they continued on together toward the store.
related_events: Scotty thanks Benny again while walking down the block
Benny teases Scotty about his black eye
Benny suggests stopping at the 5 & 10 to buy baseball supplies
Scotty agrees to stop at the 5 & 10 for supplies

name: Scotty Lies About Chewing Tobacco
description: Benny asks Scotty if he dips chaw. Scotty, not knowing what it means but eager to seem like he fits in, confidently says, 'Sure. A'course.' Benny doesn't respond, and they continue walking toward the 5 & 10.
related_events: Benny asks Scotty if he chews tobacco
Scotty confidently lies about chewing tobacco

name: HAM's Home Run into the Forbidden Backyard
description: DENUNEZ throws two pitches, both strikes. HAM swings hard and connects, sending the ball soaring into deep right field. The ball lands in a fenced backyard behind green fiberglass panels. SCOTTY tracks it and sees it drop out of sight. The gang falls silent, then begins to leave, heads down. SCOTTY steps toward the fence. The others shout, rush over, and pull him back. They warn him to stay away. BENNY tells SCOTTY to go slowly and peek through a hole in the fence. SCOTTY moves forward as the others retreat, and he brings his eye close to the hole.
related_events: DENUNEZ pitches two strikes to HAM
HAM hits a powerful swing at the pitch
THE BALL is hit deep to right field
THE BALL lands in a fenced backyard

name: Scotty Tries to Retrieve the Ball
description: After the gang starts packing up and walking away in disappointment, Scotty stands still, then makes a decision. He calls out that he’ll get the ball and takes a step toward the fence. The gang erupts in alarm, shouting for him to stop. They rush over, grab him, and pull him back ten feet. Squints stares at him, wide-eyed, saying he could’ve been killed. Yeah-Yeah chimes in, shocked at what Scotty just did.
related_events: THE GANG begins leaving the field in dejection
SCOTTY decides to retrieve the ball
SCOTTY announces he will get the ball
THE GANG reacts in panic and restrains SCOTTY
SQUINTS warns SCOTTY about the danger of the fence
YEAH-YEAH expresses disbelief at SCOTTY's action

name: The Gang Warns Scotty About The Beast
description: After Scotty asks how they’ll get the ball back, Benny stops him, warning him not to go into the backyard. The others hush him, their voices dropping. They stand together, heads down, as Benny tells Scotty to move slowly and peek through a hole in the green fiberglass fence. Scotty approaches, presses his eye close to the opening. The gang stays behind, silent. Benny says the game is over. They’ll get a new ball tomorrow. Denunez adds that the old one is gone, just a memory now. The others whisper one word: The Beast.
related_events: BENNY warns SCOTTY against returning to the backyard
THE GANG whispers about The Beast
BENNY declares the game over and proposes a new ball tomorrow
DENUNEZ dismisses the ball as a memory

name: The Gang Accepts the Ball Is Lost
description: Timmy and Repeat say they won’t get the ball back. Bertram adds that it’s gone. Ham insists it’s gone forever. Denunez calls it a memory and says to forget it. Benny announces the game is over and suggests they get a new ball tomorrow.
related_events: TIMMY and REPEAT declare the ball lost
BERTRAM states the ball is gone
HAM emphasizes the permanence of the loss
DENUNEZ dismisses the ball as a memory
BENNY declares the game over and proposes a new ball tomorrow

name: Scotty Peers Through the Fence
description: After the gang warns Scotty about the backyard, Benny tells him to move slowly toward the fence and look through a hole in the green fiberglass panels. Scotty steps forward while the others stay back. He brings his eye close to the hole and looks inside.
related_events: BENNY instructs SCOTTY to cautiously observe through the fence
SCOTTY peers through the hole in the fence

name: Benny Rodriguez Hits and Escapes the Pickle
description: Benny Rodriguez steps up to the plate and swings hard as the pitcher delivers. The ball flies deep into right field. Benny takes off, sprinting around first and then second, moving fast toward third. The throw comes in from right field, cutting him off at home. Caught in a rundown between third and home, he darts back and forth, faking one way and darting the other, dodging the catcher and third baseman. With a sudden burst, he breaks for home and slides in safely just as the tag swings wide. The radio behind the backstop crackles to life, and Squints yanks the earplug out. "Thirty-one!" he shouts. "Maury Wills just stole number thirty-one!" The opposing team throws their gloves in frustration. "Crap! Can't beat that guy!" one yells. "Why'd ya get him in a pickle? Ya know he's the damn pickle king!"
related_events: Benny Rodriguez hits a deep ball to right field
Benny Rodriguez runs the bases and gets caught in a pickle
Benny Rodriguez scores safely at home plate

name: Benny Escapes the Rundown with Feints and Speed
description: Benny Rodriguez found himself caught in a rundown between third and home after the ball was thrown in from right field. The catcher and third baseman closed in, trying to tag him out. From behind the chain-link backstop, Yeah-Yeah, Ham, DeNunez, Timmy, Bertram, and Squints rushed onto the field, crowding the basepath and shouting encouragement. Benny darted back and forth, faking one way and sprinting the other, using quick steps and sharp turns to throw the defenders off balance. He broke toward home, dashed past the outstretched glove of the catcher, and slid across the plate just as the throw arrived. He was safe. The team erupted, tossing their gloves in frustration. Nearby players on the opposing team groaned, blaming each other for trapping him in the first place. "Ya know he's the damn pickle king!" one shouted. Benny rejoined his teammates, who slapped his hand, spat pretend chaw, and skinned five like the big leaguers. Squints pulled out his pee-chee folder and recorded the stats. "Game over. Sixteen zip. Murderers' Row remains undefeated," he said. The lunch bell rang. As the group walked back toward the bungalows, an opponent yelled, "All your moms wear boxers!" Without turning, eight middle fingers shot up into the air. Nearby, Scotty Smalls stood watching, nervous and silent.
related_events: Teammates crowd the basepath and cheer for Benny
Benny Rodriguez outmaneuvers catcher and third baseman in rundown

name: Squints Announces Maury Wills' 31st Stolen Base
description: As Benny crosses home plate, safe from a rundown, Squints yanks the earplug from his transistor radio and shouts that Maury Wills has just stolen his thirty-first base. The gang erupts, celebrating both Benny’s slick move and the milestone from the majors. Squints flips open his pee-chee folder and jots down the stat as the opposing team groans in frustration. The kids mimic big league players, spitting and slapping gloves, before heading off across the playground as the lunch bell rings.
related_events: Squints hears Maury Wills steals thirty-first base on radio

name: Opposing Team Reacts After Benny Scores
description: After Benny crosses home plate, the players on the opposing team throw their gloves in all directions, their arms flailing in frustration. One of them shouts, "Crap! Can't beat that guy!" Another yells at his teammates, "Ya dufuses, why'd ya get him in a pickle for?!" They mutter about Benny being the 'pickle king' and curse his 'rubba legs,' shaking their heads as they acknowledge his speed and skill. The argument spills out onto the field, voices overlapping in disbelief and blame.
related_events: On-field team expresses frustration by throwing gloves
Opposing team blames each other for Benny's success

name: Benny Joins the Gang After the Game
description: After the play, Benny rejoined the group near the backstop. Yeah-Yeah handed him his glove. The boys mimicked big leaguers, spitting pretend chaw and slapping five. Squints pulled out his pee-chee folder and wrote down the game’s stats. The scoreboard stood at sixteen to zero. The opposing team protested, yelling that they never got their turns, but the bell rang for lunch. The gang walked off the field together toward the bungalows. Behind them, the other team shouted insults. Without turning, eight of the boys flipped them the bird. Nearby, Scotty Smalls watched nervously from the edge of the playground.
related_events: Benny Rodriguez joins the baseball gang
Yeah-Yeah gives Benny Rodriguez his glove
Gang members imitate professional baseball players
Squints records game statistics in his pee-chee folder

name: The Gang Heads Back to Class After the Game
description: The lunch bell rings across the playground. The opposing team shouts that they never got their turns at bat, but the gang doesn't respond. Benny, Yeah-Yeah, Ham, DeNunez, Timmy, Bertram, and Squints walk away together, heading back toward the bungalows. As they go, each of them flips a middle finger over their shoulder without looking back. Scotty Small, still standing near the field, watches them leave.
related_events: Opposing team protests lack of batting turns
Lunch bell rings signaling end of playground activity
Gang walks back to bungalows after game

name: Scotty Smalls Watches the Game
description: Scotty Smalls stands nearby, watching the game unfold. He stays apart from the others, his eyes following the players as they celebrate Benny's run. His posture is tense, his hands tucked close, as he observes the team shouting, spitting, and slapping hands. He doesn't move toward them, staying quiet and still while the group gathers their gloves and heads across the playground after the bell rings.
related_events: New-kid Scotty Smalls observes the game nervously

name: Benny Brings Scotty to the Game
description: Benny leads Scotty onto the baseball field, the team already gathered and warming up. The boys turn to look as Benny announces Scotty is playing. Bertram immediately questions why Scotty is there, pointing out they only needed eight players. Benny replies that with Scotty, they have nine—enough for a full team. Bertram scoffs, saying his sister could make nine too, but he didn’t bring her. Ham chimes in, lamenting that Elswenger, their former teammate, could actually throw, unlike Scotty. DeNunez agrees, calling Scotty unfit for the game. Timmy reminds Benny he already covers all the empty positions since Elswenger left. Benny insists he’ll rotate through eight spots now instead of seven and needs the practice. Squints calls the idea stupid, calling Scotty an 'L-7 weenie.' Yeah-Yeah adds, 'Oscar Mayer even.' Benny fires back, mocking Squints’ catching and running, asking why he gets to play but Scotty doesn’t. No one answers. The group heads onto the field, casting suspicious glances at Scotty, who stands apart, unsure. Benny approaches and tells Scotty to take right field. Scotty agrees eagerly but asks where that is. Benny points. Scotty runs to the spot. DeNunez takes the mound. Benny steps up to bat. He hits a pop fly toward right field. The ball drops near Scotty, who fumbles, glove raised, and misses it by several feet. The team groans. Scotty retrieves the ball and jogs it back to the pitcher instead of throwing it. The boys stare in disbelief. Scotty returns to his position. Benny walks over. He tells Scotty he can throw, but Scotty says he doesn’t know how. He thanks Benny for including him but says he should go. Benny stops him, saying he thinks too much. He asks if Scotty ever had a paper route. Scotty says he helped once. Benny tells him to throw like he’s chucking a newspaper—just let go when his arm comes around. Scotty nods. As Benny turns away, Scotty calls out, asking how to catch. Benny tells him to just stand there, glove up—he’ll handle the rest. Benny walks back toward home plate, studies the distance, rubs the ball, and tosses it into the air.

He lunges forward, grabs the ball, and stumbles back ten feet before stopping. With the others watching, he throws the ball back. It arcs low, drops quickly, and lands only a few feet ahead, rolling slowly until it stops at DeNunez’s feet. The gang bursts into laughter. Scotty turns and walks away, head down.

name: Benny Tells the Truth About Babe Ruth's Nickname
description: The gang is still laughing at Scotty's weak throw when Ham, Bertram, and Squints start tossing out their own ideas about how Babe Ruth got his nickname—each more ridiculous than the last. Benny stands quiet, then speaks up, cutting through the noise. He tells them how, as a boy, Babe was sent to a strict school, alone and scared, and when bigger kids picked on him and beat him up, he cried. The bullies started calling him 'The Babe' to mock him, a name that stuck. The yard goes completely still. No one moves or speaks. The jokes die. After a long moment, Benny turns without a word and walks away from the sandlot, leaving the others standing in silence.
